# uptimepage_status_page (Resource)

A status page: its own subdomain slug, branding, who can open it, and a curated set of monitors (added with uptimepage_status_page_component).

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "uptimepage_status_page" "public" {
  slug    = "acme"
  name    = "Acme Status"
  enabled = true

  display_name    = "Acme Status"
  about           = "Live status of Acme's public services."
  brand_color     = "#0a7cff"
  style           = "default"
  show_powered_by = true

  website_url      = "https://acme.example"
  hide_from_search = false
}

# Only the people on the list can open this one: anyone at the partner's
# domain, and one outside contractor.
resource "uptimepage_status_page" "partners" {
  slug    = "acme-partners"
  name    = "Acme Partner Status"
  enabled = true

  access = {
    protected = true
    email = {
      session_days = 30
    }
    rules = ["partner.example", "k.lindner@example.org"]
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Operator-facing page name.
- `slug` (String) Globally-unique slug that routes the public page's subdomain. Lowercased by the API.

### Optional

- `about` (String) Public 'about' blurb shown on the page.
- `access` (Attributes) Who can open the page. With `protected = true` only the people `rules` names can: anyone else gets a sign-in screen, and a listed person signs in with a code emailed to them. Making a page private removes its webhook subscribers and the email subscribers the list does not cover, and needs a plan with private pages and a server that has them; opening one works on any plan. Omit to manage access in the console instead: the provider then neither reads nor changes it, and removing it leaves the page's access as it is, so set `protected = false` to open the page to everyone again. Who signed in, and blocking them, stay in the console. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--access))
- `brand_color` (String) Accent color as a 6-digit hex like `#3b82f6`. Omit to choose the color in the console instead; a new page uses the configured brand color. Removing it keeps the color it set; clear it in the console to go back to the configured one.
- `display_name` (String) Public header name. Falls back to the org name when unset.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the page is published (publicly reachable).
- `hide_from_search` (Boolean) Serve the page, its incident pages and its feed with `noindex`. The URL keeps working for anyone who has it. Omit to keep whatever the page already has, so a page hidden from the console is not republished by an apply.
- `locale` (String) Language of the page's own labels, dates and subscriber emails, one of `en`, `de`. Text you write is shown as written. Omit to choose the language in the console instead; a new page starts in English. Removing it keeps the language it set, so set `en` to switch back. Needs a server with page languages.
- `show_powered_by` (Boolean) Pin the 'powered by' footer on or off. Omit to inherit the deployment default. Honoured only on plans that sell white-label; elsewhere the badge renders whatever this says.
- `style` (String) Visual theme. Omit to choose the theme in the console instead; a new page starts on `default`. Removing it keeps the theme it set, so set `default` to switch back.
- `website_url` (String) Your own site. The page header links here, so a reader who arrived from it can get back. `http(s)` only, at most 200 characters.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Status page id (UUID).
- `logo_url` (String) Versioned public logo URL, or null when no logo. Upload via the UI.
- `status_url` (String) Live public URL of the page, or null when no public surface is mounted.

<a id="nestedatt--access"></a>
### Nested Schema for `access`

Required:

- `protected` (Boolean) Only the people `rules` names can open the page. False opens it to everyone, and the list stays stored as `rules` gives it, for next time.
- `rules` (Set of String) Who can open it, up to 500: an address such as `anna@example.com`, or a domain such as `example.com` for every address there. Written in lower case, an internationalised domain in its `xn--` form. `[]` empties the list.

Optional:

- `email` (Attributes) The emailed sign-in code, and the passkeys that shortcut it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--access--email))

<a id="nestedatt--access--email"></a>
### Nested Schema for `access.email`

Optional:

- `passkeys_enabled` (Boolean) Let a viewer save a passkey after an email sign-in and use it next time.
- `recheck_days` (Number) Ask a passkey viewer for an email code again once they last proved their address longer ago than this: 30, 90 or 365 days. Omit to never ask.
- `session_days` (Number) Keep a sign-in for 7, 30 or 90 days. Omit to keep it until the viewer signs out, is blocked, or the list stops covering them.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Status pages are imported by their id (UUID).
terraform import uptimepage_status_page.public 0192f3a4-5b6c-7d8e-9f01-23456789abcd
```
